name: taxpayer reference number
note: Gibraltar's sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Taxpayer Identification Numbers', the jurisdiction's own sheet, with the Commissioner of Income Tax as its contact), read 2026-10-30 (saved by wave 13 the same day). The Income Tax Office issues taxpayer reference numbers, the equivalent of a TIN, to individuals and corporate entities liable to taxation in Gibraltar, for income tax and corporation tax. They consist of numerals only, assigned chronologically. The sheet sets no length, so the form gives the fewest (one digit) and no most, the pattern digits only, rather than a length guessed from any example. Read as given on registration with the Income Tax Office of a person liable to tax (the sheet says to whom, not the step; as Saint Kitts and Nevis's file reads the same words), to anyone so liable (the sheet sets no citizenship or residence). No check, age, fee or time is stated, and the sheet doesn't say what needs one, so `needed` is left out. The sheet says no specific information on the numbers is published online; the Income Tax Act 2010 it points to wasn't read for them.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Gibraltar: Information on Taxpayer Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: The Gibraltar Income Tax Office issues taxpayer reference numbers to individuals and corporate entities that are liable to taxation in Gibraltar. A taxpayer reference number is the equivalent of a taxpayer identification number (TIN). ... Gibraltar’s taxpayer reference numbers (taxpayer identification numbers) consist of numerals only, assigned chronologically.
